task.title: Page due finite recurrence occurrences
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/903 by projecting one bounded exact-recurrence page through an inclusive caller-owned cutoff without reading ambient time.
acceptance_criteria: Return complete occurrences in authored order only while instants are at or before the inclusive cutoff.
Distinguish temporary future horizons from finite completion with a resumable first-uninspected cursor.
Preserve bounded allocation, strict selected-definition replay, and typed missing or out-of-range failures.

attempts.diagnostic: Kernel integration tests failed because RecurrenceStore::due_occurrences_page did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the acceptance contract before adding production behavior.

attempts.diagnostic: Added strict exact-definition loading and bounded canonical projection through the caller-supplied cutoff.
attempts.patch: Added strict exact-definition loading and bounded canonical projection through the caller-supplied cutoff.

attempts.diagnostic: Independent review and the substantive automated walkthrough found no actionable defect; the exact one-commit head passed the Rust quality gate.
attempts.patch: Reused occurrence projection, OccurrencePageSize, store errors, and page-result contracts. Reran the complete repository quality gate after the exact implementation state was ready.

outcome.summary: Callers can deterministically page due coordinates and resume at a later cutoff without confusing a future horizon with finite completion.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0182-due-recurrence-paging.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 185 records: 185 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: A due cursor must identify the first uninspected authored coordinate so a later cutoff resumes without rescanning.
The cutoff remains explicit caller authority; the kernel must not read a wall clock or invent catch-up policy.
Inclusive cutoff behavior and finite-end behavior require separate boundary assertions.
Read-only due projection persists no cursor or provenance and grants no materialization, dispatch, retry, or execution authority.
